key_insight: A neural network potential trained on first-principles data can accurately capture oxygen-vacancy formation and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3, overcoming the scale limits of direct DFT molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables reliable, computationally efficient defect-transport simulations for perovskite oxides, supporting better materials design for devices where oxygen vacancies affect performance.
method: Trained an NNP on AIMD/DFT reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Validated energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes.
Ran large-scale, long-time NNP molecular dynamics to extract vacancy diffusion coefficients and migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP reproduces DFT reference properties and yields a vacancy migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV, close to the experimental 0.67 eV.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality and coverage of the DFT training set, so extrapolation to conditions outside the sampled defect states, temperatures, or compositions should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
